title: AEF 1.0: shared definitions
description: Definitions the other AEF 1.0 schemas reference. Not a document of its own.

schemaVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. A writer emits the version it implements; a reader accepts any minor of a major it knows and refuses an unknown major.

id.description: An identifier: 1-128 characters, letters, digits and . _ : -

ref.description: A typed reference, kind:name (for example agent:support/support-triage, suite:support/triage-scenarios).

sha256Hex.description: A SHA-256 digest: 64 lower-case hex characters (the in-toto digest form).

sha256Uri.description: A SHA-256 digest with its algorithm: sha256:<64 lower-case hex>.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 date-time in UTC, ending in Z, with up to nine fraction digits. The pattern is the rule; format is an annotation.

resultId.description: r_ + the first 32 lower-case hex characters of SHA-256 over runId, caseId, path and trial joined by U+001F, where an absent trial is the empty string (RES-4).

evidenceId.description: The id of an evidence record, unique in its run: E- and then 1-64 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' (EVD-1).

state.description: A node's state (RES-1): passed (the only pass), failed, warn (a soft failure), inconclusive (measured, undecided), scored (measured, no pass/fail rule applied), and the typed absences not_measured, not_applicable, skipped, error and pending. Closed for major 1 (VER-9).

trustedIdentity.description: An identity and the assurance its writer claims for it, as in an overlay event's by. A reader shows the assurance only as far as it verified it (OVL-3).

identity.description: Who: a stable opaque identity is recommended (an OIDC subject, a SPIFFE id, a key id) rather than an e-mail address (spec 08, SEC-4).

assurance.description: What the writer claims: self-attested, signed (a batch signature verifies for this identity) or authenticated (a host authenticated it). A reader shows it only as far as it verified it (spec 04, OVL-3).

ext.description: Producer extensions. Readers ignore what they do not know; nothing in the contract depends on it.

text.description: A name with no control character (C0, DEL, C1): caseId and path, which a result id joins with U+001F.

uri.description: A URI: a lower-case scheme, a colon, then printable ASCII without spaces; at most 2048 characters.

exactVersion.description: An exact version: printable ASCII without spaces, at most 128 characters, compared byte for byte. 'latest' (any case) is never a version: it is resolved before anything runs.

duration.description: An ISO 8601 duration of days, hours and minutes (ENC-9): P, then optionally <n>D, then optionally T and <n>H, <n>M or both in that order; each n one to five digits; at least one part, and no T without one: P14D, PT36H, PT90M, P1DT12H30M.

runRef.description: A sealed run a checkpoint lane used: its id, its run hash (frozen evidence), and where it came from.

runId.description: The run's runId, as its run.json gives it (CKP-2).

runHash.description: The run's run hash, which freezes the exact sealed files the lane relied on (CKP-2).

origin.description: launched: run for this checkpoint; adopted:<source>: an existing sealed run that matched the exact version and the comparability requirements.

relativePath.description: A path inside a run folder: segments of ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' separated by single slashes; no leading slash; no segment that starts or ends with '.' (so no '.' or '..'); at most 255 bytes. Case clashes and Windows reserved names are a rule across files (spec 03, RUN-3).

provider.description: Where a run executes: local, docker, k8s, or ci:<name> for a CI system. A runner refuses a plan whose provider it does not know or support (PLAN-7).

integer.description: Written as plain digits; a reader takes an integral number such as 2.0 as 2.

severity.description: How bad a failure is, from none to critical (spec 03, RES-9). Where a rule needs the severity of a failure that has none, it is critical.

runPointer.description: One sealed run, exactly: its id and its run hash (spec 04, SEAL-4).

runId.description: The run's runId, as its run.json gives it.

runHash.description: The run's run hash: the SHA-256 of its seal manifest, which identifies its exact content (SEAL-4).

axis.description: A comparability axis: a part of run.json two runs must agree on to be compared (spec 05, LANE-6).
